tool_args.rationale: Five measurements at one horizon show y/u_now is nearly constant, but this cannot distinguish an open-branch mechanism from an Andrade law whose horizon dependence is confounded at fixed H. Acquire the targeted open-branch probe rather than committing to an underidentified model.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the authorized Andrade power-law creep model
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: All current rows share the same H, so c0 and beta are not separately identifiable; the apparent proportionality to u_now cannot establish the horizon dependence needed for forecasting.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the authorized second-order decay model
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Its output is bounded by x_now, whereas every observed y substantially exceeds x_now, so it conflicts with the measurements.
Useful for separating horizon effects, but the current evidence already disfavors the second-order candidate; an open-branch probe is more valuable for resolving the remaining mechanism ambiguity.
